body.name: Make select(...) support prefix matches as well
Add support for hidden file input elements
body.body:
Websites often have hidden file input elements. Helium previously was not able to interact with them. Now it can. For example, via:

    attach_file('.../path/to/your/file.txt')

body.name: Improve LookupError
body.body: Previously, when you did `click("non-existent")` you received a `LookupError` without further information. Now, you get `LookupError: "non-existent"`. Similarly for other actions. This makes debugging easier.

body.name: Fix relative searches
body.body: The previous release 6.0.0 was not able to find `Button('Duplicate Button', to_left_of=Button('Duplicate Button', below=Button('Duplicate Button')))` in the following arrangement: This release fixes this. It changes which elements are found and is therefore a major version.

body.name: Improve the behavior of find_all
body.body: `find_all` had the following bug: Imagine you have the following code: ``` for label in find_all(Text('Label')): print(Link(to_right_of=label).href) ``` The bug was that this used _the same_ `Link` for each `label`, producing output for links that actually were not `to_right_of` the `label` in the loop. Furthermore, this release also changes the behavior of `find_all` in the following way. Say you have four buttons in a 2x2 grid: Previously, the following code used to return two buttons: ``` find_all(Button("Duplicate Button"), below=Button("Duplicate Button")) ``` (Namely, the two buttons in the second row, because they are both under a "Duplicate Button"). Now, this only returns one button (the first button in the second row). If you want both, you can still do: ``` for button in find_all(Button("Duplicate Button")): find_all(Button("Duplicate Button", below=button)) ``` This release is a major version bump (6.x.x) because it changes the elements returned by Helium's API and may therefore be backwards-incompatible.

body.name: Prevent Chrome's leaked password detection
body.body: Recent Chrome versions have a feature that sometimes brings up a blocking prompt _The password you just used was found in  a data breach_. This can interfere with automation. This release prevents it from being used.

body.name: Fix start_firefox(..., profile=profile)
body.body: Thank you @Jo-Blade for the [PR](https://github.com/mherrmann/helium/pull/132)!

body.name: Add support for input type=date and ...=time
body.body:
See https://github.com/mherrmann/helium/commit/2100561745de5236b585665ef8ed1271d8c0d771.

This is a minor version upgrade (5.0.... -> 5.1....) because the new implementation may find slightly different text fields.

body.name: Fix a small bug in find_all(...)
body.body: It was introduced in v5.0.5.

body.name: Fix NoSuchElementException print(...)ing elements outside the current frame
body.body: Please see the newly added test for details.

body.name: Fix error "FramesChangedWhileIterating" in wait_until
body.body: It sometimes happened. Now, `wait_until(...)` handles this error gracefully by just waiting a little more.

body.name: Switch to Selenium Manager for webdriver management
body.body:
This bumps Selenium from < 4.10 to >= 4.16, which introduces a backwards-incompatible change: `start_chrome(...)` used to take a `capabilities` parameter. This is no longer supported by Selenium. Instead, you have to use `set_capability(...)` as follows:

```
from helium import start_chrome
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options

options = Options()
options.set_capability('goog:loggingPrefs', {'performance': 'ALL'})
start_chrome(options=options)
```

body.name: Switch from Selenium 3 to 4
body.body: Thank you @tbp105 and @petrisorionel for the [amazing contribution](https://github.com/mherrmann/selenium-python-helium/pull/114)!

body.name: Fix: Helium sometimes "found" too many elements
body.body: See the new automated test `test_find_all_nested_search_areas` for an example of how it was broken.

body.name: Fix caching of chromedriver in start_chrome(...)
body.body: Since release 3.2.4, `start_chrome(...)` always used to download `chromedriver` again.

body.name: Fix error when starting Chrome
body.body:
The error was

```
get_chrome_driver.exceptions.VersionError: Unable to find a ChromeDriver version for the installed Chrome version
```

It was caused by our dependency for webdriver management not supporting current Chrome versions.

The drawback is that the new webdriver management solution doesn't cache properly. See https://github.com/SergeyPirogov/webdriver_manager/pull/582.

body.name: Fix: find_all() sometimes returned elements twice
body.body: This could happen when iframes were involved and changed during Helium's search process.

body.name: Fix an error in start_chrome
body.body: There was an error when no compatible `chromedriver` was on `PATH`.

body.name: Download chromedriver automatically
body.body:
Previous releases of Helium shipped with the `chromedriver` binaries, which are necessary for starting and controlling Chrome. But these binaries got outdated very quickly. This release switches to an approach that automatically downloads a matching `chromedriver` when none is installed on the system.

Kudos to @zaironjacobs for the [nice library](https://github.com/zaironjacobs/get-chrome-driver) that makes this possible.

body.name: Fix urllib3 error
body.body:
`start_chrome(...)` failed with the following error:

```
ValueError: Timeout value connect was <object object at 0x...>, but it must be an int, float or None.
```

This happened because Selenium 3 depends on `urllib3`, but is incompatible with `urllib3 >= 2`.

body.name: Add `profile` to start_firefox(...)
body.body: Thank you @a-l-e-c for the [PR](https://github.com/mherrmann/selenium-python-helium/pull/97)!

body.name: Add `maximize` and `capabilities` to start_chrome(...)
body.body:
These options let you start the Chrome window maximized, or pass a `DesiredCapabilities` object for further customizations.

Thank you @tarunjarvis5 and @petrisorionel for the PRs!

body.name: Fix StaleElementReferenceException
body.body: This exception spuriously occurred in some automation scripts.

body.name: Update to ChromeDriver 89.0.4389.23
body.body: Thanks @avinashtechlvr for the PR!

body.name: Use gecko/chromedriver from PATH
body.body:
Helium ships with its own copies of gecko- and chromedriver. These binaries quickly become outdated. Previously, there was no easy way to "fix" Helium's webdrivers for your machine.

No longer. Now, Helium first attempts to use `chromedriver` and `geckodriver` from your `PATH`. This lets you install the versions of those drivers that work on your system.

The implementation is based on a PR by @TotallyNotChase. Thank you!

body.name: Improve support for dragging between `Point`s
body.body: See the new test [`test_drag_point`](https://github.com/mherrmann/selenium-python-helium/blob/ffdac9349ba52d74ec45da1cc12880a5170dcbaf/tests/api/test_point.py#L95-L99).

body.name: Make it possible to supply FirefoxOptions to start_firefox
body.body: Thank you @ftnext for the PR!

body.name: Make it possible to supply ChromeOptions to start_chrome
body.body:
Added an argument `options` to `start_chrome(...)`. You can use it to supply the `ChromeOptions` when starting the browser. For example:

```python
from selenium.webdriver import ChromeOptions
options = ChromeOptions()
options.add_argument('--start-maximized')
options.add_argument('--proxy-server=1.2.3.4:5678')
start_chrome(options=options)
```
